'''Ramachandran Balasubramanian''' (born 15 March 1951) is an Indian [[mathematician]] and was Director of the [[Institute of Mathematical Sciences, Chennai|Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] in [[Chennai, India]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.imsc.res.in/about/newpage.html |title=IMSc Brochure |access-date=2009-02-07 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090310004308/http://www.imsc.res.in/about/newpage.html |archive-date=10 March 2009 }}</ref> He is known for his work in [[number theory]], which includes settling the final g(4) case of [[Waring's problem]] in 1986.<ref>Balasubramanian, Ramachandran; [[Jean-Marc Deshouillers|Deshouillers, Jean-Marc]]; Dress, François, ''Problème de Waring pour les bicarrés. I. Schéma de la solution.'' (French. English summary) [Waring's problem for biquadrates. I. Sketch of the solution] Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences, Série I 303 (1986), no. 4, pp. 85-88</ref><ref>Balasubramanian, Ramachandran; Deshouillers, Jean-Marc; Dress, François, ''Problème de Waring pour les bicarrés. II. Résultats auxiliaires pour le théorème asymptotique.'' (French. English summary) [Waring's problem for biquadrates. II. Auxiliary results for the asymptotic theorem] Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences, Série I 303 (1986), no. 5, pp. 161-163</ref> He is also known for his work in [[Cryptography]] which includes his famous work with Koblitz, now commonly called the ''Balu-Koblitz Theorem''.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Balasubramanian |first=R. |last2=Koblitz |first2=Neal |date=March 1998 |title=The Improbability That an Elliptic Curve Has Subexponential Discrete Log Problem under the Menezes—Okamoto—Vanstone Algorithm |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1007/s001459900040 |journal=Journal of Cryptology |volume=11 |issue=2 |pages=141–145 |doi=10.1007/s001459900040 |issn=0933-2790}}</ref> His work in [[Arithmetic combinatorics|Additive Combinatorics]] includes his two page paper on additive complements of squares, hence disproving a long standing conjecture of [[Paul Erdős|Erdős]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Balasubramanian |first=R |date=1988-05-01 |title=On the additive completion of squares |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0022314X88900893 |journal=Journal of Number Theory |volume=29 |issue=1 |pages=10–12 |doi=10.1016/0022-314X(88)90089-3 |issn=0022-314X|url-access=subscription }}</ref><!--, proving that there are only finitely many solutions to [[Goormaghtigh conjecture|a conjecture by Goormaghtigh]]--><!--I don't know if this is actually notable or just happens to have a Wikipedia article about it-->

His works on moments of Riemann zeta function is highly appreciated and he was a plenary speaker from India at ICM in 2010. He was a visiting scholar at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in  1980-81.<ref name="ias">{{cite web
 |url          = http://www.ias.edu/people/cos/users/rbalasubra01
 |title        = Community of Scholars Profile: Balasubramanian, R.
 |publisher    = [[Institute for Advanced Study]]
 |access-date  = 27 September 2012
 |url-status   = dead
 |archive-url  = https://web.archive.org/web/20151125100012/https://www.ias.edu/people/cos/users/rbalasubra01
 |archive-date = 25 November 2015
 |df           = dmy-all
}}</ref>

He was a student of [[Kanakanahalli Ramachandra|K. Ramachandra]], a lifelong collaborator of [[Jean-Marc Deshouillers]], and co-authored stellar mathematicians like [[M. Ram Murty|Ram Murty]], [[V. Kumar Murty|Kumar Murty]], [[Roger Heath-Brown|Heath-Brown]], [[Neal Koblitz|N. Koblitz]] and [[Florian Luca|F. Luca]]. He was the founder and remains a member of the advisory board of the [[Hardy-Ramanujan Journal]].

==Awards and honours==
He has received the following awards:
*The [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]] in 1990.
*The French government's [[Ordre National du Mérite]] for "furthering Indo-French cooperation in the field of mathematics" in 2003.<ref>{{cite news| url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/articleshow/36596631.cms | work=The Times Of India | title=French honour mathematician Balasubramanian | date=5 February 2003}}</ref>
*The [[Padma Shri Awards (2000-2009)#2006|Padma Shri]], the fourth highest civilian award in India, in 2006.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://india.gov.in/myindia/padmashri_awards_list1.php|title=India at a Glance|work=india.gov.in|access-date=4 March 2015}}</ref>
*Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]], 2012.<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2012-11-03.</ref>
*The [http://www.rediff.com/news/report/pm-honours-four-n-scientists-with-lifetime-achievement-awards/20130115.htm Lifetime Achievement Award, 2013] awarded by Manmohan Singh, the Prime Minister of India.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rediff.com/news/report/pm-honours-four-n-scientists-with-lifetime-achievement-awards/20130115.htm|title=PM honours 4 N-scientists with lifetime achievement awards|date=15 January 2013|work=rediff.com|access-date=4 March 2015}}</ref>
*Fellow of the [[Indian National Science Academy]] (1988)<ref name="Indian Fellow">{{cite web | url=http://www.insaindia.org.in/detail.php?id=N88-0985 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160813010804/http://www.insaindia.org.in/detail.php?id=N88-0985 | url-status=usurped | archive-date=13 August 2016 | title=Indian Fellow | publisher=INSA | date=2016 | access-date=May 13, 2016}}</ref>
